# Plain language checklist

| Check | Looks like | Suggest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Point buried | The ask appears in the last paragraph | Move the point or ask to the first two sentences |
| Long sentences | Over about 25 words, several clauses | Split into two sentences |
| Jargon and acronyms | "Leverage our synergies", "per the SLA" with no definition | Plain words; define an acronym on first use |
| Vague words | "soon", "a few", "some issues" | A date, a number, the specific issue |
| Unneeded passive | "Mistakes were made by the team" | "The team made mistakes" |
| Filler | "I just wanted to reach out to", "please note that" | Cut |
| Nominalizations | "make a decision", "provide an update" | "decide", "update" |
| Hedging overload | "might possibly perhaps" | One qualifier, or none |
| Wall of text | Paragraphs over five lines | Break up; use a list for steps or options |
| Weak headings | "Background", "Misc" | Headings that say something: "Why returns rose" |

## Inclusive language

| Avoid | Prefer |
| --- | --- |
| "guys", "manpower", "chairman" for a mixed or unknown group | "everyone", "staff" or "workforce", "chair" |
| "he" for an unknown person | "they", or rephrase |
| "crazy", "lame", "blind spot" as idioms | "surprising", "weak", "gap" |
| Assumptions about age, family or culture | Neutral statements |

## Accessible text

- Link text says where it goes ("pricing page"), not "click here".
- Headings in order, without skipping levels.
- Images and charts need alt text or a sentence describing them.
- Meaning is not carried by color alone ("items in red").
- Aim for text a busy reader can follow in one pass.
